content_text: The Independent Spirit Awards, sometimes translated as the Independent Spirit Award (in the original English: Film Independent Spirit Awards (also abbreviated as "Spirit Awards" and originally known as FINDIE or Friends of Independents Awards)), have been presented annually since 1984 to independent filmmakers. Winners were typically awarded acrylic glass pyramids containing suspended strings representing the small budgets of independent films. Since 2006, winners have received a metal trophy depicting a bird with outstretched wings perched on a pillar, with the shoelaces from the previous design braided around it.

In 1986, the event was renamed the Independent Spirit Awards. Now called the Film Independent Spirit Awards, the ceremony is organized by Film Independent, a nonprofit arts organization that also produces the Los Angeles Film Festival and whose mission is to champion creative independence in visual storytelling and to support a community of artists who embody diversity, innovation and uniqueness of vision. In November, its members vote to determine the award winners, who are honored the following year. Known for their credibility, the awards have become a bellwether for the Oscars when it comes to independent films in the race.

content_text: The awards ceremony is held in a tent on the beach in Santa Monica, California, usually the day before the Oscars (since 1999; originally on the preceding Saturday), and is broadcast live by the IFC television network, as well as by Hollywood Suite in Canada and by A&E in Latin America.

title: From 2021 to 2026
description:
In August 2022, Film Independent announced that the film acting categories would no longer be divided by gender. Starting with the 38th edition, in March 2023, the four categories (lead actor and actress, supporting actor and actress) were replaced by Best Lead Performance and Best Supporting Performance, with ten nominees each, and the Best Breakthrough Performance category was created.

In 2021, the awards began to include television categories (such as Best New Scripted Series), which are not shown here. Since 2023, the ceremony, which for decades aired on IFC, has been streamed live on Film Independent's and IMDb's YouTube channels.
